Full Assurance of Faith
FUL uh-SHOOR-uns uv FAYTH
noun phrase
From the Greek plērophoria pisteos, full conviction or settled certainty of faith; the believer's confident drawing near to God.

Biblical Definition

The full assurance of faith is the settled, well-grounded confidence whereby the believer draws near to God through Christ, resting upon the sufficiency of His blood and intercession. The writer to the Hebrews exhorts, let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Paul desires that the saints' hearts be comforted, being knit together in love, unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ. This assurance is not presumption, nor a fleeting feeling, but a confidence built upon the promises of God, the finished work of Christ, and the inward witness of the Spirit. It rests first upon the objective ground of the gospel—Christ crucified, risen, and pleading—and is confirmed by the subjective evidences of grace within and the testimony of the Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are the children of God. Such assurance does not belong to the essence of saving faith, so that a true believer may walk for a season without it; yet it is the privilege and proper fruit of faith, to be diligently sought through the means of grace. It produces holy boldness before the throne, peace amid trial, and a heart enlarged for obedience and worship. The full assurance of faith is therefore the settled rest of the soul upon Christ, a confidence that emboldens the saint to draw near, knowing he is accepted in the Beloved.

Webster 1828 Definition

The settled confidence whereby the believer draws near to God, resting on Christ's finished work.

FULL ASSURANCE OF FAITH, noun phrase. From the Greek plērophoria pisteos, full conviction or settled certainty of faith.

The well-grounded confidence of the believer in drawing near to God through Christ.

Built upon the promises of God, the finished work of Christ, and the witness of the Spirit.

Hebrews 10:22 exhorts, "Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience."

A privilege and fruit of faith, distinct from its essence, to be diligently sought.

Key Scripture

Heb 10:22 — "Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water."

Col 2:2 — "That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the acknowledgement of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ;"

Rom 8:16 — "The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God:"

2Ti 1:12 — "For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day."

Modern Corruption

Assurance is reduced to mere feeling, or denied to believers, or presumed upon by the unregenerate.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Yet assurance is variously corrupted within the church. Some reduce it to a passing emotional feeling, so that confidence rises and falls with the moods of the soul. Others deny that any believer may be assured at all, leaving the saints in perpetual doubt and robbing them of their birthright of peace. And many among the unregenerate presume upon a false assurance, resting in a bare profession while their lives betray no grace.

To recover the truth we must ground assurance where Scripture grounds it—upon the promises of God, the finished work of Christ, and the witness of the Spirit, confirmed by the evidences of grace within. It is not the essence of faith, so a true believer may lack it for a season; yet it is the proper fruit of faith, to be sought through the diligent use of the means of grace. So the saint examines himself, but rests his confidence not on himself but on Christ, drawing near with boldness to the throne of grace.

Hebrew Roots

Full assurance rests on God's promises, Christ's work, and the Spirit's witness, confirmed by grace within.

Assurance is a settled confidence, not a fleeting feeling or presumption.

Its objective ground is the gospel: Christ crucified, risen, and interceding.

Its subjective confirmation is the Spirit's witness and the evidences of grace.

It is not the essence of faith, so a believer may lack it for a season.

It is the privilege of faith, to be sought through the means of grace.

Usage

"The believer draws near to the throne of grace in the full assurance of faith."

"Pastors press the saints to seek assurance through the diligent use of the means of grace."

"True assurance produces boldness, peace, and an enlarged heart for obedience."
